subject: CedarWay production: checkout latency spike and 5xx increase
messages:
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@cedarway.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: CedarWay Ops <ops@cedarway.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Prod degradation — checkout latency spike & 5xx

Sean,

We're seeing a significant uptick in checkout latency for a subset of customers (p95 tokens up from ~120ms to ~900ms) and a rise in 5xx errors starting ~08:30 UTC. This is causing timeouts in our payment flow and impacting live transactions. Attached is a short sample of error lines from our side.

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2
- Impact: ~12% of checkout traffic (steady over last 45m)
- Symptoms: proxy 502/504, long DNS resolve times, occasional connection resets

Can you triage? This is high priority for us — our CS teams are getting inbound from Merchants.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Wu
SRE Lead, CedarWay
[attachment: cedarway_error_log_0803.txt (text/plain)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@cedarway.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Aug 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod degradation — checkout latency spike & 5xx

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the logs. I’ve opened an urgent investigation and looped in infra and support. Initial ask: can you confirm whether you deployed any network or proxy rules in us-west-2 in the last 2 hours? Also please share a packet capture (pcap) if available.

Our immediate plan:
- Marissa and Vanessa will look at serving telemetry and edge traces for the affected model endpoints.
- Jonas will work on escalation playbook and exec notification if this looks like a cross-customer routing issue.
- I’ll keep your team updated every 30m until we have a mitigation.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@cedarway.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Aug 2028 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod degradation — checkout latency spike & 5xx

Looping in our infra triage notes — early signals from runtime:
- Token serialization times fine; most latency is in TCP connect + TLS handshake (p95 ~800ms).
- We see a cluster of DNS timeouts from a small set of egress NAT IPs in us-west-2.
- Correlated increase in proxy 502/504 originating at an upstream proxy pool.

Immediate checkpoints:
1) Vanessa: can you pull peering and NAT metrics for the affected pools (packet drops, conntrack usage)?
2) Neha: verify whether any model variant rollouts hit these nodes (unlikely but checking).
3) Alex: if you can confirm whether your ops ran a proxy rule change, that will help narrow scope.

Attaching a short trace we pulled from a sample request.
[attachment: redwood_trace_0803.pcap (pcap)]

I'll follow up with concrete mitigation in 20–30m.

—Marissa
Senior Incident Lead, Redwood Inference

From: CedarWay Ops <ops@cedarway.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Wu <alex.wu@cedarway.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Aug 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod degradation — checkout latency spike & 5xx

Marissa / Sean,

We did a targeted change to an egress proxy access-list at 08:18 UTC to block a set of IP ranges that were misbehaving; that change involved a short ACL reload on our proxy fleet around 08:20–08:25. We’re seeing a correlation between that window and the first spike.

We’re attaching an expanded set of logs and a note from our network team — the ACL was intended to drop only outbound calls to known bad hosts, but it looks like some long-lived connection patterns from Redwood’s NAT pool matched the rule and were reset.
[attachment: cedarway_error_log_0803_full.txt]

We can roll back the ACL immediately if that helps; what’s your recommendation?

—CedarWay Ops

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Aug 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod degradation — checkout latency spike & 5xx

Summary / proposed exec steps (for Sean):
- Likely root cause: CedarWay introduced an egress ACL reload that matched Redwood NAT IPs -> TCP resets and DNS failures, producing higher handshake times and proxy 502s.
- Scope: impacts CedarWay production in us-west-2 only; limited to customers routed through affected proxy pool (~12% of their traffic).
- Immediate mitigation options:
  1) CedarWay rolls back the ACL change (fastest) — they offered rollback.
  2) Redwood can route CedarWay traffic to an alternate NAT pool / fallback region for 30–60m (we can push a targeted routing override).
  3) Short-term: increase connection keepalive and aggressive DNS retry on the affected endpoints (code patch riskier).
- Recommended: do (1) + (2) in parallel. If CedarWay rolls back, we still provision fallback routing for safety.

Action items:
- Sean: coordinate rollback with Alex and confirm when done.
- Marissa / Vanessa: prepare canary route + monitoring (ready in ~20m).
- Neha: prepare postmortem template and list of impacted customers.
- Jonas: draft exec note + proposed credit language if SLA breach is confirmed.

I’ve prepared a short mitigation playbook (attached).
[attachment: mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf]

—Jonas
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@cedarway.com>, CedarWay Ops <ops@cedarway.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Aug 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Prod degradation — checkout latency spike & 5xx

Alex / Ops — quick status and resolution summary.

Timeline & root cause:
- 08:18 UTC: CedarWay applied targeted egress ACL reload.
- 08:20–09:05 UTC: Rising connection resets and DNS timeouts observed; p95 handshake rose to ~900ms, 5xx spiked to ~14%.
- 09:10 UTC: CedarWay rolled back the ACL; partial recovery observed within ~8 minutes.
- 09:20 UTC: Redwood deployed targeted routing override for CedarWay traffic to alternate NAT pool as a safety net. Full recovery to baseline by ~09:40 UTC.

Impact: transient SLO breach for CedarWay checkout traffic in us-west-2; estimated customer-facing impact window ~40m.

Next steps:
- Joint postmortem scheduled: 2028-08-06 10:00 UTC (calendar invite sent).
- CedarWay to share final proxy ACL diff and remediation plan.
- Redwood to produce RCA and credit proposal draft for review by legal/procurement.

Thanks for the quick collaboration here — the rollback + routing override stopped further impact. Jonas, please escalate this to the account execs and attach the proposed credit language.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference
